item.text: I’m narrowing this wave to the highest-value items: UN/OHCHR, OVD-Info, Memorial, SOVA, FIDH/HRW, and the strongest local-language pieces on detention, anti-war repression, and the Dagestan antisemitism crisis. The scholarship item is probably duplicate/low-priority, but I’ll verify the public sources first.

**New Accepted Records**

- `3B-S096` [Violence in Queer Families: Symbolic Recognition of Same-Sex Relationships in Russian Law](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10896-023-00630-7) | Springer / Journal of Family Violence | 2023-08-25 | source type: scholarship | source confidence: high, because it is peer-reviewed, open access, and based on nine Russian criminal court cases | final evidence use: structural evidence on queer-family violence, legal recognition, and hostile legal discourse | language: en | locator: [`turn9view9`](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10896-023-00630-7) lines 52-61, 95-107 | factual claims: the study analyzes nine intimate-partner violence cases in queer families; most cases involve lesbian/bisexual women; courts recognize same-sex relationships only in criminal-violence processing; the article argues this recognition remains subordinate and pathologizing under “traditional values” rhetoric | temporal fit: not a 2023 incident report, but relevant structural context for the 2023 chapter | ruler attribution: legal discourse and courts under the Putin-era state | inherited/context limits: indirect evidence; use for legal-social environment rather than direct state violence counts | contrary considerations: the article also notes some formal recognition inside criminal proceedings, so it is not purely one-directional | lenses: 3B.3, 3B.5, 3B.7

- `3B-S097` [Russian wartime repression report. One year since the full-scale invasion](https://data.ovd.info/russian-wartime-repression-report-one-year-full-scale-invasion) | OVD-Info | 2023-02-23 | source type: rights monitoring | source confidence: high, because it gives quantified anti-war repression data and abuse descriptions from a specialist monitor | final evidence use: target-period baseline for repression scale, custody, and police abuse | language: en | locator: [`turn4view0`](https://data.ovd.info/russian-wartime-repression-report-one-year-full-scale-invasion) lines 72-74; [`turn2view0`](https://data.ovd.info/russian-wartime-repression-report-one-year-full-scale-invasion) lines 87-88, 91, 94 | factual claims: OVD-Info counted almost 20,000 anti-war arrests across 240 locations in 78 regions; 447 people were prosecuted and 125 were in custody; police used force, beatings, and strangling; women arrested at protests were subjected to sexual violence in some stations | temporal fit: direct target-year and immediate post-invasion evidence | ruler attribution: national police, prosecutors, and the anti-war legal regime | inherited/context limits: aggregate monitoring with some undercount risk, especially for hidden custody abuse | contrary considerations: the report is protest-focused, so it captures repression more than the full domestic safety picture | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10

- `3B-S098` [Wartime Repressions Report. August 2023](https://ovd.info/en/anti-war-repression-report-august-2023) | OVD-Info | 2023-08-30 | source type: rights monitoring | source confidence: high, because it provides updated counts and specific examples of anti-war detention through August 2023 | final evidence use: mid-2023 repression scale and ongoing protest suppression | language: en | locator: [`turn4view1`](https://ovd.info/en/anti-war-repression-report-august-2023) lines 65-75 | factual claims: OVD-Info says an unprecedented wave of repression began after the invasion; it knew of 19,096 detentions during protests and 326 after them, plus 364 detentions for online posts, symbols, private conversations, and related reasons; 8,609 detentions involved women | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: police, courts, and the wartime control regime | inherited/context limits: data are cumulative to August 20, 2023 and may undercount hidden cases | contrary considerations: the report includes some cases where detainees were released without protocol, but that does not offset the scale | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10

- `3B-S099` [The New Generation of the Far-Right and Their Victims. Hate Crimes and Counteraction to Them in Russia in 2023](https://www.sova-center.ru/en/xenophobia/reports-analyses/2024/02/d47069/) | SOVA Center | 2024-02-14 | source type: scholarship / monitoring | source confidence: high, because it is a specialist annual hate-crime report with concrete counts and attack examples | final evidence use: vulnerable-group violence and state-environment context | language: en | locator: [`turn9view1`](https://www.sova-center.ru/en/xenophobia/reports-analyses/2024/02/d47069/) lines 62-72; [`turn8view5`](https://www.sova-center.ru/en/xenophobia/reports-analyses/2024/02/d47069/) lines 129-133 | factual claims: SOVA recorded 18 LGBT+ victims in 2023, up from 6 in 2022; people associated with LGBT+ were threatened; a Moscow attack injured seven people near the Ostankinsky district court; homophobia worsened amid the official fight against LGBT propaganda | temporal fit: strong for 2023 and immediate follow-up | ruler attribution: not all violence is state-directed, but the legal and rhetorical environment is state-shaped and relevant to tolerance/failure to protect | inherited/context limits: hate-crime report, not a direct government record | contrary considerations: some violence is far-right or informal rather than direct state action, so attribution must be capped accordingly | lenses: 3B.3, 3B.7, 3B.9, 3B.10

- `3B-S100` [Russia: Amid a wave of antisemitic violence in the North Caucasus, authorities must ensure the protection of the local Jewish community](https://www.fidh.org/en/region/europe-central-asia/russia/russia-amid-a-wave-of-antisemitic-violence-in-the-north-caucasus) | FIDH | 2023-11-06 | source type: NGO / monitoring | source confidence: high, because it documents a specific domestic crisis and calls for independent investigations and protection | final evidence use: crisis-response failure and minority-protection evidence | language: en | locator: [`turn9view2`](https://www.fidh.org/en/region/europe-central-asia/russia/russia-amid-a-wave-of-antisemitic-violence-in-the-north-caucasus) lines 47-58; [`turn4view5`](https://www.fidh.org/en/region/europe-central-asia/russia/russia-amid-a-wave-of-antisemitic-violence-in-the-north-caucasus) lines 59-60, 67 | factual claims: after the Dagestan airport riot and related incidents, FIDH said the Russian authorities needed to protect the Jewish community and carry out independent investigations; the airport mob searched for Jewish passengers, shouted antisemitic slogans, and forced passengers to hide or be evacuated | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: federal and regional authorities, especially their failure to prevent or rapidly contain the violence | inherited/context limits: press release format, but grounded in a specific crisis with concrete incidents | contrary considerations: the press release itself does not document the state response in detail, so it mainly establishes the need for protection and the severity of the incident | lenses: 3B.3, 3B.7, 3B.9, 3B.10

- `3B-S101` [Russia: Inadequate Response to Antisemitism in North Caucasus](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/11/09/russia-inadequate-response-antisemitism-north-caucasus) | Human Rights Watch | 2023-11-09 | source type: institutional monitoring | source confidence: high, because it gives concrete incidents and a direct critique of the authorities’ failure to protect Jews in the region | final evidence use: crisis-response failure, anti-Jewish violence, and inadequate remedy | language: en | locator: [`turn9view3`](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/11/09/russia-inadequate-response-antisemitism-north-caucasus) lines 608-610; [`turn5view7`](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/11/09/russia-inadequate-response-antisemitism-north-caucasus) lines 611-613; [`turn2view7`](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/11/09/russia-inadequate-response-antisemitism-north-caucasus) lines 625-626 | factual claims: HRW says Russian authorities failed to respond adequately to antisemitic acts in the North Caucasus; incidents included an airport mob hunting Israeli passengers, a hotel attack, and arson at a Jewish community center; police made some arrests but broader accountability was unclear; Putin told officials to protect constitutional order and inter-ethnic accord, but HRW still judged the response inadequate | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: federal and regional authorities; Putin’s instructions show formal top-level attention, but not effective remedy | inherited/context limits: some incidents were later or still unfolding at publication time | contrary considerations: the article includes a limited positive element, namely arrests and an ongoing airport investigation, but says these were insufficient | lenses: 3B.3, 3B.7, 3B.9, 3B.10

- `3B-S102` [Gay man detained at Moscow airport on Chechnya’s request, handed over to security services and taken to an unknown location](https://theins.ru/en/news/259426) | The Insider | 2023-02-15 | source type: local-language reporting | source confidence: medium-high, because it relies on NC SOS reporting and describes a concrete disappearance-risk custody transfer | final evidence use: Chechen security-service abuse and minority persecution | language: en | locator: [`turn3view8`](https://theins.ru/en/news/259426) lines 24-26 | factual claims: Idris Arsamikov, a gay man from Chechnya, was detained at Moscow’s Domodedovo airport, taken away by Chechen security services, and believed at risk of torture and death; a Chechen officer allegedly had previously tortured him with electric shocks | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: Chechen security services and the broader federal tolerance structure that allowed the transfer | inherited/context limits: the report is a rights-advocacy relay and the strongest claim is about risk and prior abuse, not a fully adjudicated disappearance case | contrary considerations: the alleged future harm is inferred from prior conduct and NC SOS assessment | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.7, 3B.8

- `3B-S103` [Chechen singer Zelimkhan Bakayev murdered by security forces as his homosexuality “offended” Ramzan Kadyrov, reports NC SOS crisis group](https://theins.press/en/news/263716) | The Insider | 2023-07-25 | source type: local-language reporting | source confidence: medium, because it reports a grave allegation from NC SOS and eyewitnesses rather than a concluded court finding | final evidence use: severe anti-LGBTQ violence and state-aligned impunity context | language: en | locator: [`turn9view4`](https://theins.press/en/news/263716) lines 27-37 | factual claims: the piece says Bakayev disappeared in 2017 after traveling to Grozny and was killed by Chechen security forces, according to NC SOS; Chechen authorities denied involvement; activists linked the case to a broader hunt for homosexuals in the region | temporal fit: historical allegation, but still relevant as background on a 2023 domestic-safety lens | ruler attribution: Chechen security forces and the Kadyrov-aligned local system, with federal tolerance implications | inherited/context limits: allegation-heavy, not independently adjudicated in the article itself | contrary considerations: the claim is contested by Chechen authorities and should be treated as a serious allegation rather than established fact | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.3, 3B.7, 3B.10

- `3B-S104` [“Называли фашисткой, предательницей и позором страны”](https://verstka.media/detey-presleduyut-za-antivoennuyu-poziciyu) | Verstka | 2023-02-14 | source type: local-language reporting | source confidence: high, because it gives a concrete case and states the breadth of repression against minors | final evidence use: repression of children and families for anti-war expression | language: ru | locator: [`turn8view0`](https://verstka.media/detey-presleduyut-za-antivoennuyu-poziciyu) lines 35-36 | factual claims: Russian security services pursued not only adults but also teenagers and children for anti-war protests and posts; a Moscow fifth-grader and her mother were taken to police over a pro-Ukrainian avatar and school dissent; at least seven minors became criminal defendants | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: police, Center “E,” and guardianship officials under the wartime repression regime | inherited/context limits: a feature article, but the underlying incidents are concrete | contrary considerations: none that materially soften the pattern; the article is one-sided but specific | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10

- `3B-S105` [“Мне стыдно за своё поколение, это оно во всём виновато”](https://verstka.media/sotni-rossiyskih-pensionerov-osuzhdeny-ili-oshtrafovany-za-protesty-protiv-voyny) | Verstka | 2023-08-15 | source type: local-language reporting | source confidence: high, because it uses OVD-Info data and concrete sentencing examples | final evidence use: breadth of anti-war punishment across age groups | language: ru | locator: [`turn8view1`](https://verstka.media/sotni-rossiyskih-pensionerov-osuzhdeny-ili-oshtrafovany-za-protesty-protiv-voyny) lines 35-36 | factual claims: more than 200 pension-age Russians had been convicted for anti-war actions or statements since February 24, 2022; some were sent to colonies despite serious illness; fines were far beyond pension income | temporal fit: strong target-year evidence | ruler attribution: police, courts, and the anti-war legal regime | inherited/context limits: counts are cumulative from the invasion onward and may not isolate 2023 alone | contrary considerations: the article includes some public-opinion context, but the core evidence is punitive enforcement | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10

- `3B-S106` [Россиян стали чаще судить за «гостайну» и антивоенную позицию](https://verstka.media/gosizmena-inoagenty-voennye-statistika-sudov-2023) | Verstka | 2024-04-19 | source type: local-language analysis | source confidence: high, because it is grounded in court-department statistics and reports concrete shifts in prosecutions | final evidence use: 2023 court-statistics context on anti-war and control offenses | language: ru | locator: [`turn9view7`](https://verstka.media/gosizmena-inoagenty-voennye-statistika-sudov-2023) lines 35-36, 62-76, 79-83 | factual claims: in 2023 Russian courts convicted 555,743 people; prosecutions increased for state-secrets disclosure and anti-war positions; 478 administrative cases targeted foreign-agent compliance; 115 people were convicted for repeated “discrediting” or wartime “fake” speech; military courts issued a record number of convictions, including many for unauthorized absence and violent crimes by servicemen | temporal fit: target-period statistical follow-up | ruler attribution: courts and the legal regime under Putin | inherited/context limits: statistics article, not a direct human-rights monitor, and some figures reflect system-wide criminal justice rather than only political repression | contrary considerations: it notes fewer domestic-violence protocols, but that is not a reliable safety signal by itself | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.10

- `3B-S107` [Activist arrested for spreading pro-Ukrainian leaflets dies in detention center in Russia](https://theins.ru/en/news/262573) | The Insider | 2023-06-15 | source type: local-language reporting | source confidence: medium-high, because it reports a custodial death and torture allegation via OVD-Info and the lawyer | final evidence use: custody death, torture risk, and brutality of administrative detention | language: en | locator: [`turn9view8`](https://theins.ru/en/news/262573) lines 24-26 | factual claims: Anatoly Bereznikov died in a Rostov-on-Don detention center after being held for anti-war leafleting; his lawyer said he had been tortured with a stun gun the day before his death and had received threats | temporal fit: direct target-year evidence | ruler attribution: detention-center staff, police, and the administrative detention system | inherited/context limits: single case, but highly salient for detention abuse and lethal risk | contrary considerations: the torture allegation is reported through counsel, so the custodial death is firmer than every detail of the abuse narrative | lenses: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.5, 3B.9, 3B.10

**Remaining Gaps**
- Direct evidence of effective civilian oversight, complaint handling, and meaningful remedy is still thin.
- Evidence that Putin reduced domestic fear without replacing it with state fear remains weak.
- Broader protection evidence for women, children, and non-LGBT vulnerable groups is still under-supplied.
- Some of the strongest minority-protection and detention-abuse sources here are allegation- or advocacy-driven, so attribution must stay calibrated.
- The accepted pool is now broad enough for chapter drafting, but the weakest lenses remain `3B.4` and `3B.6`.
